rationale: C05 plausibly supplied a concrete template for the child: both are short presidential messages celebrating an American's distinguished victory abroad, asserting that Americans share pride in the achievement, and connecting the individual's success to international friendship. C22 and C11 contain related congratulatory or international-understanding structures, but their occasions and language are less closely aligned.

shared_material.child_excerpt: I know that all Americans join with me in paying tribute to his artistic talents and are proud that he was awarded first prize
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Millions of Americans would like to participate with the New Yorkers today... We are proud of you not only as a great competitor and a master of your craft
shared_material.explanation: Both present the President as voicing the shared pride of Americans in a highly skilled winner returning from an international triumph.

shared_material.child_excerpt: I believe such contests are good for a better understanding between people of all nations.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: an envoy extraordinary in the business of building friendship for America
shared_material.explanation: Both close the praise by treating the honoree's international competitive success as a contribution to friendship or understanding among nations.

shared_material.child_excerpt: When he returns to the United States, I hope he can come to the White House so that I can congratulate him personally on his triumph.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: extending their traditional welcome upon your return from your magnificent victory
shared_material.explanation: Both frame the message around welcoming home and congratulating an American after a major victory abroad.
